BiblicalUsage: Sarag is things twisted and wrapped together, like sinews or a yoke. The behemoth moves his tail like a cedar, and the sinews of his stones are wrapped together; and my own transgressions are wreathed and come up upon my neck, too heavy to rise under.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sin wraps itself around a person the same way, strand by strand, until only God can lift the weight off.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
